evals.name: write-tests-command
evals.prompt: in /tmp/cc-fixture (kotlin gradle project) make me a slash command /write-tests that takes a kotlin file path and writes good unit tests for it, runs them, and tells me coverage gaps
evals.expected_output: Project command file with frontmatter (description, argument-hint), skeleton blocks, routes to testing-expert skill, verify step runs gradle tests, explicit output block.

evals.name: ship-workflow-side-effects
evals.prompt: turn my pre-push routine into a user-level command: I run ./gradlew detekt, then ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest, if both green I write a conventional commit msg for staged changes, commit, and push to current branch. call it ship
evals.expected_output: User-level command with disable-model-invocation true, fail-fast stops on red detekt/tests, routes commit message to a commit skill (e.g. caveman:caveman-commit), narrow allowed-tools, pre-injected git context.

evals.name: audit-verbose-code-review
evals.prompt: /tmp/cc-fixture/.claude/commands/code-review.md is bloated generic junk I copied from github. rewrite it so its tight and actually useful, reviewing only my current diff
evals.expected_output: Rewritten command on skeleton, much shorter, scoped to current diff via !`git diff` injection with allowed-tools, routes to a review skill, severity-ranked output block, before/after line count reported.
